internal.title: Incident Report: Cart Service Elevated Error Rate Due to Feature Flag Error Injection
internal.body:
At 11:18 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for the cart service due to a 100% error rate and elevated latency. Investigation identified that a recent feature flag change ('cartFailure') was enabled at 100%, which injected errors causing the service disruption. CPU and memory metrics ruled out resource exhaustion as a cause. The flag was disabled at 11:38 UTC after approval, leading to immediate recovery and normalization of error rates.

Timeline:
- 11:18:54: Alert received for high error rate in cart service.
- 11:38:39: Diagnosis confirmed error injection due to 'cartFailure' flag.
- 11:38:45: Flag disable command proposed, approved, and executed.
- 11:38:45: Recovery verified with error rates returning to normal.

Root Cause: Error injection from the 'cartFailure' feature flag.
Resolution: Disabled the 'cartFailure' flag, restoring service functionality.

Lessons learned and action items are documented to prevent recurrence.

external.title: Intermittent Cart Service Errors Resolved
external.body: Between 11:18 and 11:38 UTC on November 8, some customers experienced errors when using the cart service. The issue was caused by a feature update that unintentionally introduced errors. The update was quickly rolled back, and the service has returned to normal operation. We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your understanding.

lessons.lesson: Feature flag changes should be carefully staged and monitored to prevent full-scale service disruptions.

action_items: Implement stricter controls and staged rollouts for feature flags affecting critical services.
Enhance monitoring to detect error injections from feature flags earlier.
